deadline_text_verbatim: Deadline: November 2
limitations: No year stated on the live page. This is CMU's actively-maintained, current prospective-student-facing deadlines page, but its exact day-of-month for the Early Decision deadline does not match two OTHER official CMU sources checked in this same pass (see cross-references).
researcher_notes:
THREE independent official CMU sources give THREE different Early Decision closing dates: this live Application Plans & Deadlines page says 'November 2' (undated); the course catalog (coursecatalog.web.cmu.edu), explicitly self-dated 'entering in fall 2026', says 'November 3' (see DL0002, VERIFIED_HISTORICAL, cycle_year 2026); the Common Data Set 2025-2026 (Section C21) says 'November 1' (see DL0003), and is corroborated by the College of Fine Arts Applicants page's Architecture/Art/Design-specific 'Apply and submit your portfolio by November 1' (also 'November 1'). All three are official cmu.edu-domain sources. This is recorded per this lane's evidence rule 5 (conflicts recorded, never silently resolved) and the founder brief's explicit instruction not to pick the 'more current-looking' source. Best guess for a human reviewer: this live page is most likely to reflect the CURRENTLY open cycle (Fall 2027 entry, since Fall 2026 has already begun as of this 2026-08-21 retrieval), but that is an inference, not a sourced fact -- the page itself names no year, and the specific day has genuinely moved by 1-2 days across the sources found, so a downstream product should treat the exact day as NEEDS_REVIEW-grade rather than display it with unqualified confidence to a student.

RESOLUTION 2026-08-22 (see docs/research/requirement-conflicts/02-cmu-early-regular-decision-dates.md): NOT A CONFLICT. One rule accounts for all six disputed dates: CMU's nominal deadlines are 1 November and 1 January, shifted to the next business day when they fall on a weekend or holiday. Fall 2026 entry (the course catalog's self-dated cycle): 1 Nov 2025 was a Saturday -> Mon 3 Nov; 1 Jan 2026 was a Thursday holiday and 4 Jan a Sunday -> Mon 5 Jan. Fall 2027 entry (this live, undated page): 1 Nov 2026 is a Sunday -> Mon 2 Nov; 1 Jan 2027 is a Friday holiday followed by a weekend -> Mon 4 Jan. The Common Data Set reports the unshifted nominal dates, which is what the CDS form asks for. Every figure is predicted; none is explained away. Live page re-fetched 2026-08-22, unchanged. LIMITATION: the course catalog URL returned ECONNRESET twice on 2026-08-22, so its figures were not re-verified.
